explicit_bias_for.reason: Incident metrics need compression and rolling aggregates.
Leadership asked about anomaly embedding search.

full_intake.free_form_notes: Incident responders need recent-window metrics, tenant isolation, and fast status timelines. There is talk of AI vector anomaly search, but no embedding corpus, offline labels, or recall target exists. The not yet posture should be explicit rather than hype.

recommendations.title: Constraints
triggers_for_next_stage: Escalate to exclusion constraints or RLS when overlap or tenant-isolation rules become explicit.
why_not_yet: If invariants are not yet known, start by naming the entity lifecycle and failure states before adding broad constraints.
why_now: Relational core data needs database-enforced truth before optional architecture choices.
Constraints make bad states visible across every application writer.

recommendations.title: pg_stat_statements
triggers_for_next_stage: Use top total time and calls to justify the next index, schema, or topology recommendation.
why_not_yet: Ownership is still required: reset cadence, query text policy, and review rhythm should be explicit.
why_now: Workload decisions need normalized statement evidence before adding indexes, replicas, or extensions.
pg_stat_statements is low-risk and broadly available.

recommendations.title: Row-level Security
triggers_for_next_stage: Review policy coverage for every tenant-scoped table and add plan checks for hot tenant filters.
why_not_yet: RLS policies need session identity plumbing, bypass-role review, tests, and operational debugging discipline.
why_now: Shared-schema tenancy puts tenant isolation inside every query path.
RLS gives the database a backstop when application filters are missed.

recommendations.title: Declarative Partitioning
triggers_for_next_stage: Escalate to pg_partman only after manual partition operations become a recurring operational risk.
why_not_yet: Partitioning is premature when tables are modest, retention is vague, or queries do not prune by partition key.
why_now: Large append-heavy tables need bounded maintenance, retention, and pruning strategy.

recommendations.title: BRIN for Append-only Time
triggers_for_next_stage: Add btree companion indexes only for proven tenant, status, or id filters.
Adopt when time-window scans dominate and table ordering remains correlated.
why_not_yet: It is weak when data is not physically correlated with time or queries need point lookup.
BRIN depends on physical correlation and does not replace point-lookup btrees.
why_now: BRIN is a low-maintenance fit for large chronological append-only tables.
Append-heavy chronological data often gets useful pruning from small BRIN indexes.

recommendations.title: TimescaleDB
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt with documented compression policy, continuous aggregate ownership, restore testing, and rollback criteria.
Revisit when compression, chunk maintenance, and retention automation are measured pain.
why_not_yet: Do not adopt if the managed-service target cannot support extension upgrades, restore drills, and retention runbooks.
Core partitioning, BRIN, materialized views, and scheduled retention should be measured first.
why_now: Large central time-series tables plus adjacent analytics create recurring chunk, retention, compression, and aggregate-maintenance work.
At this scale, TimescaleDB is justified only because the workload has crossed beyond one-off partition maintenance.
Very large time-series metrics may benefit from hypertable lifecycle, compression, and retention ergonomics.

recommendations.title: Composite Equality Then Range
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt after pg_stat_statements identifies repeated tenant/status/time or account/time access paths.
why_not_yet: Column order must come from real predicates, not generic indexing instinct.
why_now: Hot OLTP and read-heavy filters often need equality columns before range or sort columns.

recommendations.title: Partial Indexes
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when pg_stat_statements or EXPLAIN shows repeated filters on status, tenant, active windows, or sparse flags.
why_not_yet: Partial indexes need proven predicates; without query traces they become brittle guesses.
why_now: Large OLTP tables often have small hot subsets that should not force full-table index maintenance.

recommendations.title: Partial Index for Skew
triggers_for_next_stage: Review index size and write amplification after one representative traffic window.
why_not_yet: Wait until the predicate is stable in application SQL and selectivity has been measured.
why_now: The index catalog has a matching pattern for selective predicates on skewed large tables.

recommendations.title: Generated Columns
triggers_for_next_stage: Promote keys when query traces show stable filters, joins, uniqueness, or validation needs.
why_not_yet: Wait until the hot keys are known; generated columns should not mirror every JSON attribute.
why_now: Generated columns make repeatedly queried JSONB keys visible to constraints and indexes.

recommendations.title: GIN JSONB Containment
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt after EXPLAIN shows repeated @> predicates with selective keys.
why_not_yet: It is costly when the application does not use containment or filters too broadly.
why_now: GIN JSONB can support containment queries on flexible attributes.

recommendations.title: JSONB
triggers_for_next_stage: Promote hot JSON keys to generated or ordinary columns once query pressure and invariants are visible.
why_not_yet: Do not make the whole entity JSONB when keys are frequently filtered, joined, constrained, or audited.
why_now: JSONB can carry variable attributes while stable identifiers and lifecycle columns stay relational.

recommendations.title: Materialized Views
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when repeated aggregate queries dominate total time and stale-enough answers are acceptable.
why_not_yet: Refresh cadence, staleness tolerance, and locking behavior must be known first.
why_now: Adjacent analytics often needs precomputed read models before replicas or distributed systems.

recommendations.title: PgBouncer
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt once pool sizing, failover routing, and idle-session behavior are documented.
why_not_yet: Confirm application compatibility with transaction pooling, prepared statements, and session settings.
The rule matched, but weighted score is below the recommend-now threshold; confirm operational ownership, portability posture, and workload evidence first.
why_now: High peak connections on OLTP/read-heavy traffic should not map one application worker to one backend.

recommendations.title: Physical Replication
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when read routing, lag tolerance, and failover behavior are documented.
why_not_yet: A replica does not fix bad queries, missing indexes, or write bottlenecks on the primary.
why_now: Read-heavy systems can isolate reporting and expensive reads with replicas.

recommendations.title: Covering B-tree With INCLUDE
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when visibility map health and EXPLAIN show index-only scan potential.
why_not_yet: Covering indexes add write and storage cost, so projections must be stable and valuable.
why_now: Read-heavy stable projections may benefit from INCLUDE columns and index-only scans.

recommendations.title: PgBouncer in Front
triggers_for_next_stage: Test failover target changes and pool draining in maintenance runbooks.
Adopt after transaction duration, idle sessions, and prepared-statement behavior are measured.
why_not_yet: It cannot compensate for long transactions or inefficient queries.
Pool mode can break session-state assumptions and should be tested with the application.
The rule matched, but weighted score is below the recommend-now threshold; confirm operational ownership, portability posture, and workload evidence first.
why_now: Putting PgBouncer in front makes connection admission a topology concern.
Many concurrent sessions call for an explicit pooling layer in front of PostgreSQL.

recommendations.title: Expression Indexes
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt once normalized email, SKU, phone, or JSON extraction filters repeat.
why_not_yet: They depend on exact expression matching and should be tied to specific query shapes.
why_now: Expression indexes can support normalized lookup while keeping the base model compact.

recommendations.title: pg_partman
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when future partition creation or retention jobs become reviewed operational toil.
why_not_yet: The table must already deserve partitioning; pg_partman is not the reason to partition.
why_now: Recurring time-based partition creation and retention can justify pg_partman automation.

recommendations.title: Primary With Read Replicas
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when read routing, lag tolerance, and consistency expectations are explicit.
why_not_yet: Replicas inherit bad query plans and introduce lag; they are not a first fix for missing indexes.
why_now: Reporting or read-heavy traffic may need isolation from primary write latency.

recommendations.title: pgcrypto
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt when URL-safe identifiers or database-side UUID defaults are explicit requirements.
why_not_yet: Do not treat cryptographic functions as a security architecture without review.
why_now: Database-generated UUID defaults are useful for public identifiers and distributed inserts.

recommendations.title: Citus
triggers_for_next_stage: Revisit after single-primary tuning, partitioning, read replicas, and tenant-local query traces are exhausted.
why_not_yet: Do not adopt Citus until hot reads and writes consistently include a stable distribution key.
why_now: Strong tenant locality and large tables may eventually justify distributed PostgreSQL.

recommendations.title: Citus Distributed Cluster
triggers_for_next_stage: Adopt only with cluster-aware restore drills and clear shard-key ownership.
why_not_yet: Cluster backup, restore, rebalancing, and query-plan review are substantial operating costs.
why_now: The topology is plausible only if co-location and cluster operations are explicit.

recommendations.title: pgvector
triggers_for_next_stage: Revisit pgvector after an embedding corpus, offline evaluation set, and lexical or spatial baseline gaps are documented.
why_not_yet: There is no embeddings_vectors data shape, embedding refresh plan, recall target, or permission-aware retrieval design yet.
For geo-heavy logistics, PostGIS answers spatial distance and containment questions more directly than vector search.
why_now: The intake mentions semantic or vector-style search, so pgvector should stay visible as a possible later option.

recommendations.title: No Pooling With High Connections
triggers_for_next_stage: Add pool sizing, transaction duration, and session-state compatibility checks.
why_not_yet: Application pools may be enough if limits and transaction duration are already disciplined.
why_now: High peak connections without pooling evidence risks backend exhaustion and idle-session waste.

warnings.message: High peak connections without pooling evidence risks backend exhaustion and idle-session waste.
